transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’ve developed this intense, irrational fear of going into the ocean, even though I grew up surfing. It's gotten to the point where it's really starting to control my life, so I decided it was time to get some help.
Can you tell me if your fear is specifically related to the ocean itself, or is it more about what might be in the ocean, such as sharks or other creatures?

It’s definitely about the ocean itself and the power of the water, not sharks or sea creatures. My mind just goes straight to getting caught in a rip current again and being dragged under. I'm terrified of that feeling of being completely unable to fight the current.
When you think about or are near the ocean, do you experience any panic symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?

Yes, definitely. Just picturing myself paddling out makes my heart race, my chest get really tight like I can't breathe, and my legs turn to jelly. If I'm actually near the shoreline, I start sweating like crazy and find myself gripping my keys tightly just to cope.
Do you experience these panic symptoms only when you're thinking about or exposed to the ocean, or do you also have unexpected panic attacks that aren't related to your fear of the ocean?
No, it only happens when I'm thinking about the ocean or when I'm actually near the water. I've never had these panic feelings out of the blue or in any other situations.
Have you experienced any significant traumatic event related to the ocean in the past, such as a near-drowning experience, that might have triggered this intense fear?

Yes, about eleven months ago, I got caught in a sudden rip current during an early-morning surf session. It pulled me really far out from the shore before a lifeguard was able to rescue me. That incident completely shook my sense of safety in the water, which had always felt like home to me.

Did you experience any significant distress, avoidance of reminders, or intrusive memories related to the rip current incident after it happened, beyond just the development of your fear of the ocean?

Yes, but those memories and the distress are strictly tied to the ocean and the thought of going back in. When I look at the water or picture paddling out, my mind instantly jumps back to that day and I feel like I'm back in that moment, which is why I avoid the beach entirely now. Outside of ocean-related situations, I don't experience those intrusive thoughts or anxiety at all.
Can you describe if there's anything else besides the ocean and the fear of rip currents that you avoid or find distressing, or is it solely related to this specific situation?

No, it's strictly about the ocean and anything connected to it, like surfing, walking on the beach, or attending shoreline events. There isn't anything else in my life that triggers this kind of intense fear or avoidance.

Did the intense fear of the ocean develop immediately after the rip current incident, or was there a period of time where you were able to surf or be near the ocean without significant distress before the fear became overwhelming?

The fear started pretty much right after the incident eleven months ago. At first, I tried to convince myself that I just needed a temporary break to recover, but I was never actually able to get back in the water without panicking. I immediately started turning down surf invitations and trips because the anxiety was just too intense.
Have you noticed any significant reduction in your fear or anxiety related to the ocean over the past eleven months, or has it remained relatively consistent or even intensified?

No, it hasn't let up or gotten any better at all over the past eleven months. The fear and anxiety have remained consistently intense since the incident, and they haven't reduced even a little bit. It still feels just as strong today as it did right after it happened.
Have you tried any coping mechanisms or strategies to overcome your fear and anxiety related to the ocean, or sought any professional help before coming here today?

I haven't sought professional help before this, but I've tried to cope by avoiding the beach entirely—parking blocks away, making excuses, and throwing myself into gaming or extra shifts at the barber shop. I'm only here now because my uncle suggested it after I couldn't bring myself to join a family ceremony on the shoreline and stayed in the parking lot instead.

You've mentioned that your fear and anxiety have remained consistently intense since the incident eleven months ago, but can you tell me if there are any specific aspects of your daily life, beyond just surfing or being near the ocean, that have been significantly impacted by this fear, such as relationships, work, or other hobbies?

It's been incredibly frustrating because this fear has completely cut me off from my friends, my cultural responsibilities, and my own identity as a water-person. Missing that major family ceremony at the shoreline because I couldn't leave the parking lot was a huge blow, and it made me realize how much I'm isolating myself. Now, I just try to distract myself by taking on extra shifts at the barber shop or hiding at home playing video games, which is really damaging my self-image.
Can you describe if you experience any significant emotional numbing, guilt, or shame related to the rip current incident itself, beyond the fear and anxiety of the ocean?

No, I don't really feel any emotional numbing, guilt, or shame about the incident itself. My feelings are mostly just focused on the intense fear and anxiety of the ocean, and a lot of frustration over how much this is messing up my life.

You mentioned frustration and fear, but can you tell me if you've experienced any persistent and pervasive negative emotions, such as persistent negative thoughts about yourself or the world, since the rip current incident?

I haven't really experienced any pervasive negative thoughts about myself or the world in general. My frustration and negative feelings are strictly tied to the ocean, my inability to go into the water, and feeling cut off from my identity as a water-person. Outside of that, I don't have a generally negative outlook on life.

Have you experienced any flashbacks or nightmares specifically about the rip current incident that are not just related to your fear of the ocean, but rather a re-experiencing of the traumatic event itself?
No, I haven't really had any nightmares or sudden flashbacks out of nowhere. Those intense feelings and memories only hit me when I'm actually near the ocean or actively thinking about going in.
Can you describe how you feel about the rip current incident itself, is it more about the fear of the ocean or do you have distressing memories of the event that feel like they're happening again?

It is primarily an intense fear of the ocean itself, though picturing myself paddling out does make me feel temporarily back in that helpless moment. When that happens, my heart races and my legs feel like jelly, but the core issue is that the water now feels incredibly dangerous to me. I'm just terrified of the idea of getting back in.

Can you tell me if you have experienced any avoidance of thoughts, feelings, or conversations associated with the rip current incident, or if you've tried to avoid remembering the details of what happened during that event?

Yes, I definitely try to avoid thinking or talking about it. If the topic comes up or I start picturing it, I just freeze up, feel overwhelmed, and immediately try to change the subject. To keep my mind off those thoughts, I usually just bury myself in gaming or take on extra shifts at the barber shop.

Can you tell me if the distress and impairment you're experiencing are solely related to the fear of the ocean and its power, or if you also experience significant distress when reminded of the rip current incident itself, in a way that feels like reliving the event?

The intense distress is definitely tied to the ocean and the idea of going into it. However, when I look at the water or picture myself paddling out, my mind instantly flashes back to the rip current incident, making me feel like I'm reliving that terrifying moment. When that happens, my heart starts racing, my chest gets tight, and I just completely freeze up.

Do you experience significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning that are not directly related to your fear of the ocean, such as difficulties with concentration, sleep disturbances, or irritability?

No, I don't experience any of those other issues like trouble sleeping, concentrating, or being irritable. All of my distress and the difficulties in my life are pretty much entirely tied to my fear and avoidance of the ocean.

Can you clarify if the primary issue for you is the fear of the ocean itself, or if the fear is closely tied to the memory and distress of the rip current incident, feeling like you're reliving it when you think about the ocean?

While the memory of the rip current is very strong and triggers those physical reactions, the primary issue is definitely just an intense, overriding fear of the ocean itself. Even when the water is completely calm and safe, the thought of actually getting in feels incredibly dangerous and terrifying, which is why I avoid the beach entirely.

Can you describe if there's a clear distinction for you between the fear of the ocean and the memory of the rip current incident, or do they feel closely intertwined in a way that makes it hard to separate one from the other?

They are deeply intertwined and it's really hard to separate them. Whenever I look at the ocean or even picture myself paddling out, my mind immediately jumps straight back to that moment of being dragged under by the rip current. It honestly feels like I am back in that terrifying situation all over again.

Can you tell me if you experience any feelings of detachment from others, restricted range of affect, or sense of a foreshortened future, which are not directly related to your fear of the ocean, but rather a broader impact of the rip current incident on your life and relationships?

No, I don't really experience those feelings of general detachment, restricted emotions, or a shortened future. Any feelings of being cut off or isolated are strictly because I'm avoiding the beach and ocean-related activities, rather than some broader change in my outlook on life.

Do you think that if you could overcome your fear of the ocean, the memories and distress related to the rip current incident would still significantly bother you, or would resolving the fear of the ocean also largely resolve the distress from the incident?

I'm not entirely sure, but the two feel deeply connected. Since the memory of the incident is what triggers my fear of the water, I feel like overcoming that fear would probably go a long way in resolving the distress from the memory too.

If you were to imagine yourself in a situation where you felt completely safe from the rip current, such as in a swimming pool or a controlled water environment, would your fear and anxiety about the water itself diminish, or would it persist?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about being in a pool, because all of my fear and anxiety have been entirely focused on the ocean and the beach since the incident.
If you were in a completely controlled and safe aquatic environment, like a pool, would you experience the same level of fear and anxiety as you do when thinking about the ocean?

I'm really not sure, because I haven't actually tried going into a pool since it happened. My fear has been completely focused on the ocean and that rip current incident, so I haven't really thought about how I'd feel in a different water environment.

If you were to encounter a situation where you had to be in the ocean, but with a guarantee of safety, such as being in a secure, enclosed area within the ocean, do you think your fear and anxiety would still be as intense?

Yes, I think the fear would still be just as intense. Even when I know intellectually that I'm safe—like when the waves are calm and lifeguards are right there—my body and mind still react as if I'm in extreme danger. It's so irrational and hard to control that any setup in the ocean would still trigger that strong physical panic.

If you were to encounter a situation where you had to be near or think about a different body of water, such as a lake or a river, would you experience the same level of fear and anxiety as you do with the ocean?

I haven't really thought about lakes or rivers, because my fear is entirely focused on the ocean and that specific incident with the rip current. Since I don't have any reason to go near those other bodies of water, I'm really not sure how I would react.

If you were able to completely overcome your fear of the ocean, do you think you would still experience distressing memories or flashbacks of the rip current incident, or would resolving the fear of the ocean also resolve the distress from the memory?

I'm really not sure because I haven't been able to overcome this fear yet. I'd hope that getting past the fear of the ocean would help quiet those memories, but I imagine that day might always be a bit scary to look back on.
